results.claim: The display driver only DMAs the dirty ROW range (HAL_LCDC_SetROIArea(0, s_update_y0, WIDTH-1, s_update_y1)) and converts RGB222->RGB332 in place row by row. Vertical locality of changes matters; horizontal locality does not.
results.evidence: display_jdi.c: "// Only send the dirty region that was converted to RGB332 format" then "HAL_LCDC_SetROIArea(&state->hlcdc, 0, s_update_y0, PBL_DISPLAY_WIDTH - 1, s_update_y1)"; display_update() sets s_update_y0 from the first row and s_update_y1 = row.address per row and converts "this row in-place from 222 to 332"; terminate converts "back from 332 to 222" for y in [s_update_y0, s_update_y1]. ROI always spans full width 0..WIDTH-1.

results.claim: layer_mark_dirty() only calls window_schedule_render() which sets window->is_render_scheduled = true; window_render() then calls layer_render_tree() on the ENTIRE tree. There is no per-layer dirty rectangle.

results.claim: window_do_layer_update_proc() fills the whole window bounds with the background colour on every render UNLESS gcolor_is_transparent(bg) — so window_set_background_color(w, GColorClear) is the key trick to get a genuinely small dirty-row range.

results.claim: Alloy (pure JavaScript/TypeScript SDK via Moddable XS) targets ONLY emery and gabbro — not aplite/basalt/chalk/diorite/flint. The official FAQ says to write in C when you need full platform reach or 'the smallest possible memory footprint'.

results.claim: Alloy has a hard memory ceiling: the XS machine uses a fixed 32 KB static block ('creation': {'static': 32768}) for all slots/chunks/stack. After PebbleOS 4.17.0 (Moddable 8.2.3), non-trivial Alloy apps crash at load with 'fxAbort memory full' and reboot the watch, while ~88 KB of app heap ('App bytes free = 87908') remains unreachable to the JS engine. Native C apps are unaffected.
results.evidence: Issue #1621 documents exactly this for PebbleOS 4.17.0 ('creation.static = 32768', 'App bytes free = 87908'), but it was closed 2026-07-03 after phoddie's fix ('turned the chunk and slot allocation down from 49 KB to 29 KB and it works'); commit 76cd73282 (2026-07-03) 'moddable: fix ffi memory crash and memory allocation' shipped in v4.21.0/v4.22.0. SDK 4.33 (2026-08-12) further 'Updated Moddable (Alloy) to SDK 8.3.1, bringing the XS engine to 17.8'.
results.correction: This describes a June 2026 regression that has been fixed since July 2026 (firmware 4.21+/4.22+, current firmware 4.36.0); it should not be presented as a current hard ceiling.

results.claim: The Pebble QEMU emulator needs SDL2, glib, pixman, zlib and libsndio at runtime, which the docs install via `sudo apt` — a blocker on a no-sudo machine. Serve una misura empirica (riga 'Free RAM available (heap)' del build report + heap_bytes_free()/heap_bytes_used() loggati dopo init e dopo il primo render + un probe che alloca 8/16/32/64/96 KiB in blocchi crescenti) che riconcili CONFIG_APP_RAM_EMERY_SEGMENT_SIZE=135.168 B e CONFIG_APP_RAM_EMERY_RUNTIME_SIZE=63.488 B con la frase del changelog 4.33 'loaded image and RAM footprint are still limited to 64 KiB each'; e va verificato se l'emulatore QEMU emery applica lo stesso budget dell'hardware (assunto dal piano, mai testato) e quanto heap resta dopo il framebuffer/AppState. Da questo dipende la dimensione massima di bitmap, cache offline in RAM e strutture UI: e' la decisione architetturale su cui poggia tutto il resto.

Corollario decisivo per l'offline-first: la quota persist da 1 MiB dipende dal firmware (non dall'SDK), PBL_API_EXISTS() e' un controllo di compilazione e non di runtime, quindi qual e' il pattern corretto per rilevare a runtime quota e disponibilita' API e ricadere sui 4 KiB legacy? Nessuno dei sette topic ha coperto la compatibilita' app-vs-firmware, che decide se la cache locale puo' essere dimensionata su 1 MiB.

La matrice emu-* documentata copre quick view, content size, bt-connection, battery, tap/accel/compass, steps/heart-rate ma non il touch. critic.notes:
Contraddizioni ricerca vs verifica (sintesi):

1) Versioni in movimento: la ricerca fissa il firmware a v4.35.0 (19/08); la verifica trova v4.36.0 pubblicato il 24/08. Ogni numero di firmware nel piano invecchia in giorni (minor ogni pochi giorni); SDK 4.33.1 e pebble-tool 5.0.39 restano corretti.

2) "Nessun sudo": la pagina SDK ufficiale prescrive `sudo apt install libsdl2 libglib2.0 libpixman-1 zlib1g libsndio7.0`. Il workaround dpkg-deb -x + LD_LIBRARY_PATH e' l'unica via su questa macchina, ma e' stato verificato in sandbox: nell'HOME reale non esistono ne' uv, ne' pebble, ne' ~/.local/share/pebble-sdk, ne' ~/.local/lib/pebble-deps; l'unica traccia e' /var/tmp/pebble-sdk (directory volatile). La Fase 0 va rifatta da zero nell'HOME.

3) Percorso SDK: la verifica corregge ~/.pebble-sdk -> XDG ~/.local/share/pebble-sdk. Il piano contiene un bug conseguente: il passo `mkdir -p ~/.pebble-sdk && touch NO_TRACKING` (anche nel job CI) forza la dir legacy, mentre il check `ldd`, il `--query-driver` di clangd e la cache CI puntano a ~/.local/share/pebble-sdk. Usare NO_TRACKING dentro la dir XDG.

4) Python 3.14: la raccomandazione "evitare 3.14" e' imprecisa — il fallimento e' l'assenza di ensurepip nel Python di sistema, non la versione; un 3.14 gestito da uv funziona. Resta 3.13 come scelta ufficiale.

5) Memoria emery: contraddizione non risolta fra 128 KiB (Kconfig/pebble_sdk_platform) e "64 KiB each" (changelog 4.33), piu' RUNTIME_SIZE 63.488 B. Il piano la marca come da confermare: e' il gap #1.

6) Persist: 1 MiB (verificato sul sorgente firmware) contro 4 kB ripetuti da community-examples, publishing-compat e dalla guida ufficiale stale. Vince 1 MiB, ma dipende dal firmware dell'orologio -> gap #2.

7) Alloy: il "tetto rigido di 32 KB" (issue #1621) e' una regressione di giugno 2026 gia' risolta a luglio (fw 4.21/4.22) e Alloy ha guadagnato `pebble/health` in 4.33. La scelta di C resta giusta (flint, memoria, MenuLayer/ActionBar), ma va argomentata senza quel dato ormai falso.

8) Risorse memory-mapped: CONFIG_MMAP_RESOURCES vale solo per le risorse di SISTEMA; le risorse delle app di terze parti fanno comunque malloc dell'intero file sull'heap. Nessun risparmio di RAM da li'.

9) Nomi API errati nella ricerca: sono `app_launch_button()` e `app_launch_get_quick_launch_action()` (prefisso app_). E `clock_to_timestamp()` gestisce il DST nel firmware, al contrario di quanto scritto.

10) Ecosistema sottostimato: llms.txt ufficiale esiste (HTTP 200), pebble-mcp e' su PyPI, esiste un SDK Zig community attivo (vsergeev/zig-pebble-sdk); l'estensione VS Code v0.0.8 e' del 15/02/2026 (non 18/08) e il repo e' archiviato. Dimensioni ufficiali PT2: 43,00 x 36,04 x 10,90 mm, 33 g (le cifre di terze parti erano 2016-era). "Bluetooth 5.3" non e' dichiarato da Core, solo dal brief SiFli.

11) Emulatori: la FAQ elenca 5 piattaforme, la verifica locale del piano ne dichiara 7 (flint e gabbro inclusi) — da riconfermare al primo avvio. Confermato invece che i changelog SDK 4.18-4.32 sono davvero 404 (controllati i salvataggi in scratchpad): esistono solo 4.17, 4.33, 4.33.1.

gapfills.summary: Derived from PebbleOS sources (main and tag v4.33.2, the firmware the SDK 4.33.1 emulator runs): on emery a native SDK-4.x app gets app segment CONFIG_APP_RAM_EMERY_SEGMENT_SIZE = 135,168 B, of which 4,096 B is stack+guard (APP_STACK_NORMAL_SIZE 4 KiB on emery/gabbro), leaving exactly 131,072 B (128 KiB) for loaded image + heap. The heap is therefore heap ~= 131,072 - virtual_size (.text+.data+.bss), i.e. between ~64 KiB (max static footprint) and ~128 KiB; a typical 20-35 KB watchface image yields ~95-110 KiB heap. The "64 KiB" in the SDK 4.33 changelog refers to PebbleProcessInfo.load_size/virtual_size being uint16_t (static footprint cap enforced by inject_metadata.py, app_storage.c APP_MAX_SIZE, process_loader_storage.c), not the heap; the 128 KiB binary limit only benefits the relocation table (PR #1827, issue #1873 still open). CONFIG_APP_RAM_EMERY_RUNTIME_SIZE = 63,488 B is a separate region holding AppState, including the inline 200x228x8-bit framebuffer (45,600 B), so framebuffer/AppState cost the heap nothing. The build report's "Free RAM available (heap)" = 0x20000 - (text+data+bss) coincides with the real heap within alignment bytes on emery. The allocator (lib/util/heap.c) stores block sizes in 15 bits of 4-byte units (max ~131,060 B per block), so a single malloc > 64 KiB (e.g. 96 KiB) succeeds if virtual_size <= ~32.7 KB; but heap_realloc truncates the old block size to uint16_t, so realloc on blocks >= 64 KiB silently loses data. The QEMU emery board (boards/qemu_emery/defconfig, soc/qemu/Kconfig.defconfig: SRAM 0x7fc00, PLATFORM_EMERY) uses identical APP_RAM sizes to obelix hardware. No public native-C heap_bytes_free() measurement on a real Pebble Time 2 exists; Alloy-app issues #1621/#1592 report 66-88 KB free consistent with the model. Report includes a ready-to-run probe app and no-sudo Linux setup (uv + pebble-tool; toolchain and QEMU downloaded by `pebble sdk install`).

facts.claim: Kconfig on main and at tag v4.33.2 sets APP_RAM_EMERY_SEGMENT_SIZE=135168 and APP_RAM_EMERY_RUNTIME_SIZE=63488; comment says SEGMENT = stack+text+data+bss+heap and RUNTIME = AppState, and emery/gabbro use a 4 KiB app stack with the segment sized 2 KiB larger to compensate.

app_manager.c: for a 4.x app the segment is CONFIG_APP_RAM_4X_SEGMENT_SIZE; 32 B stack guard + 4,064 B stack are carved from the top, the image is loaded at the bottom, and the remainder becomes the app heap via heap_init(); the rest of APP_RAM (RUNTIME) goes to app_state_configure().

Resulting native-app heap on emery is ~131,072 B minus virtual_size (.text+.data+.bss), i.e. ~64 KiB to ~128 KiB depending on the app's static footprint; this is a source-derived figure, not a published hardware measurement.
SDK 4.33 changelog (2026-08-12): max app binary on Emery/Gabbro is 128 KiB, but 'The loaded image and RAM footprint are still limited to 64 KiB each; the extra room is available for relocation data.'

PebbleProcessInfo.load_size and .virtual_size are uint16_t, so static footprint is capped at 65,535 B on every platform; inject_metadata.py raises 'App virtual size is N bytes ... Must be 65535 bytes or smaller' and app_storage.c checks virtual_size > APP_MAX_SIZE (0x10000).

PR #1827 (merged 2026-08-03) states explicitly: 'This does not give emery/gabbro 128 KB of application memory ... virtual_size still caps static footprint at 65535 on every platform'; a 126,932-byte image with a 15,700-entry reloc table was installed and relocated correctly in the emery emulator.

Issue #1873 (opened 2026-08-16, still open) reproduces with SDK 4.33.1: build report shows 'Total footprint in RAM: 60232 bytes / 128.0KB' yet padding .bss by 8 KB to 68,440 B fails the build with the uint16_t error; widening needs a PROCESS_INFO struct version bump and mobile-app parser changes.

The build report's 'Free RAM available (heap)' is MAX_APP_MEMORY_SIZE (0x20000 for emery) minus text+data+bss; since 135168-4096 = 131072 exactly, it matches the real heap on emery within a few alignment bytes.

AppState (in the 63,488 B RUNTIME region) contains the FrameBuffer by value with uint8_t buffer[200*228 = 45,600] on 8-bit platforms; 4.x apps get a 200x228 framebuffer; therefore the framebuffer does not consume app heap.

heap.c: block Size is a 15-bit field in 4-byte units and heap_malloc returns NULL when allocation_size >= SEGMENT_SIZE_MAX (0x7FFF), so the largest single allocation is ~131,060 B; a 96 KiB malloc is allowed by the allocator and succeeds when the heap has that much contiguous space (fresh heap at init).

heap_realloc computes 'const uint16_t original_size = heap_info_ptr->Size * ALIGNMENT_SIZE' (line 532, present on main and v4.33.2), truncating sizes >= 65,536 B, so realloc of a block >= 64 KiB copies too few bytes (silent data loss).
heap_bytes_free() = heap_size - current_size and heap_bytes_used() = current_size (bytes including block headers); it reports total free bytes, not the largest contiguous block.

boards/qemu_emery/defconfig selects CONFIG_SOC_QEMU, CONFIG_PLATFORM_EMERY, 8-bit color and MODDABLE_XS; soc/qemu/Kconfig.defconfig sets SRAM_SIZE 0x7fc00 (same as SF32LB52) with the comment 'QEMU mirrors the SRAM layout of the platform it emulates' — so the emulator applies the same app RAM budget as Pebble Time 2 hardware.
SDK 4.33.1 changelog (2026-08-14): no SDK changes; the emulator now runs firmware 4.33.2 (recognizer crash fix).

Issue #1621 (2026-06-28): an Alloy app on Pebble Time 2 hardware and the emery emulator (fw 4.17.0) reported 'App bytes free = 87908' at XS machine creation; issue #1592 reported ~66,000-70,000 free on hardware — consistent with 122,880 minus image for Moddable apps (8 KiB JS stack).

Rebble hardware table lists Emery 'Max App Size (code + heap): 128k*5' with footnote 5: SF32LB52J has 16 MB PSRAM not currently enabled in PebbleOS; PR #1602 'enable psram on emery/gabbro' (2026-06-24) was closed without merge.

Flint (Pebble 2 Duo) uses segment 67,584 + runtime 30,720 with a 2 KiB stack, i.e. 65,536 B for image+heap; tools/pebble_sdk_platform.py gives flint MAX_APP_MEMORY_SIZE 0x10000 and emery/gabbro 0x20000.

pebble-tool README: 'The toolchain (arm-none-eabi) and QEMU binary are no longer bundled, but instead installed when pebble sdk install is run'; a Linux setup verified 2026-07-12 uses 'uv tool install --force pebble-tool==5.0.39 --python 3.13' then 'pebble sdk install latest' with the toolchain landing under ~/.local/share/pebble-sdk/SDKs/<ver>/toolchain/.

recommendations: Run the probe app in the report (section 6) on the emery and flint emulators on day one: record the build report 'Free RAM available (heap)', heap_bytes_free() at main entry / after init / first render, and the outcome of malloc(8/16/32/64/96/112/120/128 KiB); then repeat with an 8 KiB static pad to confirm .bss costs heap 1:1.

Plan with the rule heap ~= 131,072 B - virtual_size on emery (65,536 B - virtual_size on flint) and set a project ceiling on static footprint (e.g. <= 40 KB) to guarantee >= ~88 KiB of heap; never rely on the '128.0KB' shown in the build report as a code budget — the real static cap is 65,535 B.
Allocate large buffers (offline cache, 8-bit bitmaps) once in init(), largest first, and never call realloc() on blocks >= 64 KiB (uint16_t truncation bug in heap_realloc); size them up front.
Always check malloc() return values (third-party apps get NULL, no croak) and degrade gracefully (e.g. fall back to 4-bit palette bitmaps).
Use heap_bytes_free() as telemetry only; to know whether a large contiguous block is available, attempt the actual malloc at startup.

Budget bitmaps by format: full-screen 8-bit = 45,600 B; prefer GBitmapFormat4BitPalette (22,800 B), 2-bit (11,400 B) or 1-bit (5,700 B) resources loaded on demand; the system framebuffer is not charged to the app heap.
Treat the emery emulator as budget-identical to hardware (same Kconfig); validate only rendering performance and timing on the physical Pebble Time 2.
Keep local arrays small: the app stack is 4,096 B including a 32 B guard on emery (2 KiB on flint).
Do not plan around >128 KiB budgets in 2026: issue #1873 (widening virtual_size) is open and PSRAM (PR #1602) is unmerged; consider filing the heap_realloc uint16_t truncation upstream.

Environment on Linux without sudo: install uv, then 'uv tool install pebble-tool --python 3.13' (or the pinned 5.0.39), 'pebble sdk install latest'; verify with ldd that the downloaded qemu-system-arm finds SDL2/glib/pixman/sndio/libpng, and if not, provide them in user space (e.g. micromamba conda-forge) via LD_LIBRARY_PATH.
open_questions: No published heap_bytes_free()/heap_bytes_used() figure from a native C app on a real Pebble Time 2 was found; the ~131,072 - virtual_size model is derived from source and from Alloy-app numbers (issues #1621/#1592), and still needs the empirical run described in the report.
Exact baseline heap consumed by the applib runtime before main() (app_message_init, app_outbox_init, etc.) on emery is unknown — expected to be small (< 1 KiB) but unmeasured.
Whether the QEMU firmware binary downloaded by 'pebble sdk install' for SDK 4.33.1 is built with CONFIG_MALLOC_INSTRUMENTATION (8 B vs 4 B block headers) could not be verified; impact is negligible.
The heap_realloc uint16_t truncation for blocks >= 64 KiB is inferred from reading lib/util/heap.c (main and v4.33.2); it has not been reproduced on device or emulator.
sizeof(AppState) on emery (must be <= 63,488 B) was not computed; only that it contains the 45,600 B framebuffer inline.
The Notion-hosted PebbleOS changelog (ndocs.repebble.com) could not be fetched; its 4.33.1 wording ('apps can now use the full 128 KB binary limit') is known only via a quote in issue #1873.
Whether Core Devices will widen virtual_size/load_size (issue #1873, open since 2026-08-16) or enable PSRAM in a future PebbleOS release is undecided.
Running the QEMU emulator on Ubuntu 26.04 without sudo depends on the downloaded binary's shared-library needs (SDL2, glib, pixman, sndio, libpng); the user-space workaround is untested.

gapfills.summary:
Answered both halves from primary sources (source code + official docs), all 2026-dated.

TOUCH IN THE EMULATOR — YES, fully emulated. The Core Devices QEMU fork (github.com/coredevices/qemu, branch pebble-10.1) contains hw/misc/pebble_touch.c, instantiated on machine `pebble-emery` (has_touch=true, 200x228, Cortex-M33), and the emulator firmware board boards/qemu_emery/defconfig sets CONFIG_TOUCH=y with src/fw/drivers/touch/Kconfig `TOUCH_QEMU default y if SOC_QEMU`. So TouchService, tap/pan/swipe recognizers and app_touch_navigation_enable() are testable without hardware.

There is NO `pebble emu-touch` and there never will be: touch does not travel on the QemuProtocol serial channel (enum stops at 13 = HeartRate, no touch entry). It enters via QEMU's input subsystem. Two working injection paths: (a) mouse click/drag in the SDL window — confirmed by source ("Receives mouse events from QemuConsole", mask BTN|ABS; ui/sdl2.c calls qemu_input_queue_abs) but undocumented anywhere in developer.repebble.com; (b) QMP `input-send-event` with abs axes + left button, exactly what `./pbl touch X Y` / `./pbl swipe` do. pebble-tool does NOT open a QMP socket — workaround: wrap the binary via PEBBLE_QEMU_PATH adding `-qmp unix:...`, or launch QEMU manually and attach with `pebble --qemu localhost:12344`. The HMP monitor pebble-tool does expose is useless (mouse_move emits REL events which pebble-touch ignores).

Also emulated: RGB backlight (display regs 0x18/0x24/0x28/0x2C), speaker/mic (audiodev sdl). HRM is a stub fed by `pebble emu-heart-rate` (protocol 13). NOT emulated: ambient light sensor, any battery power model (BATTERY_QEMU = "fixed values"), real vibration, multi-touch.

REAL PT2 FROM LINUX — no. Official FAQ says a phone is required. `--serial` is Bluetooth-Classic/SPP legacy; PT2 uses NimBLE + PPoGATT (BLE only). libpebble2/pebble-tool have no BLE transport; libpebble3 builds only android/ios. luigi311/cobble (Rust/BlueZ/PPoGATT, Linux) connects but lacks PutBytes and AppLogs, so no install and no logs.

Critical side-finding: touch is forbidden in watchfaces (SDK 4.33 guide).

facts.claim: The QEMU machine `pebble-emery` (used by pebble-tool for SDK > 4.9.148, i.e. 4.33.1) declares has_touch=true, has_audio=true, display 200x228, CPU cortex-m33, desc 'Pebble Emery (obelix, Cortex-M33)'.

hw/misc/pebble_touch.c implements device TYPE_PEBBLE_TOUCH='pebble-touch' whose header comment states 'Receives mouse events from QemuConsole and provides touch coordinates', with QemuInputHandler mask INPUT_EVENT_MASK_BTN | INPUT_EVENT_MASK_ABS and props display-width=200 / display-height=228. Therefore mouse click+drag in the SDL window IS touch input.

ui/sdl2.c sdl_send_mouse_event() calls qemu_input_queue_abs(INPUT_AXIS_X/Y) when qemu_input_is_absolute() is true, and handle_mousemotion() forwards drags; with a decoration active sdl2_decoration_map_mouse() remaps coordinates, and clicking the drawn bezel buttons synthesizes Pebble key presses via sdl2_decoration_send_button().

PebbleOS documents touch injection: './pbl touch 130 130' and './pbl swipe 130 220 130 40 --steps 20 --duration 0.4', noting 'Injection uses the absolute-pointer input path; multi-touch is not wired up in the device' and that it requires the QMP socket exposed by './pbl qemu'.

The pbl implementation of touch/swipe uses QMP: qmp_capabilities, then qom-list/qom-get walk of /machine to find the touch device and read display-width/display-height, then input-send-event with {'type':'abs',...value=px/width*32767} plus {'type':'btn','data':{'button':'left','down':true/false}}.

The QEMU protocol enum in PebbleOS ends at 13 (SPP=1, Tap=2, BluetoothConnection=3, Compass=4, Battery=5, Accel=6, Vibration=7, Button=8, TimeFormat=9, TimelinePeek=10, ContentSize=11, HealthMetric=12, HeartRate=13) and contains NO touch protocol — so no `pebble emu-touch` command can exist on that channel.

pebble-tool 5.0.39 launches QEMU with '-monitor tcp::PORT' but NO '-qmp'; the QEMU binary path is overridable with the PEBBLE_QEMU_PATH env var ('qemu_bin = os.environ.get("PEBBLE_QEMU_PATH", "qemu-pebble")'), which makes a wrapper adding -qmp the simplest fix. Emulator ports are recorded in /tmp/pb-emulator.json.
HMP 'mouse_move' cannot drive the touch device: hmp_mouse_move calls qemu_input_queue_rel(INPUT_AXIS_X/Y), i.e. relative events, which pebble-touch (BTN|ABS mask) ignores.

boards/qemu_emery/defconfig enables CONFIG_TOUCH=y, CONFIG_BACKLIGHT=y + CONFIG_BACKLIGHT_QEMU_COLOR=y (RGB backlight), CONFIG_SPEAKER=y, CONFIG_MIC=y, CONFIG_HRM=y with CONFIG_HRM_STUB=y, and does NOT enable ambient light (present only on obelix).

The emulated display device exposes backlight registers DISP_BRIGHTNESS 0x18, BL_RED 0x24, BL_GREEN 0x28, BL_BLUE 0x2C (0-255) and renders 8bpp ARGB2222 GColor8, so RGB backlight tint and brightness are visually reproduced.

Battery in QEMU is a stub: src/fw/drivers/battery/Kconfig defines BATTERY_QEMU 'Stub battery driver for QEMU (fixed values)', default y if SOC_QEMU — there is no power model, so battery/autonomy cannot be validated in the emulator.

pebble-tool 5.0.39 actually implements more emu-* commands than the published docs list, including emu-button (click/push/release with --duration/--repeat/--interval), emu-steps, emu-distance, emu-calories, emu-active-time, emu-sleep, emu-heart-rate (protocol 13) and emu-set-content-size. emu-tap is an accelerometer tap (protocol 2), not a touchscreen tap.

Touch is explicitly NOT supported in watchfaces: 'Touch input is currently not supported in watchfaces... touch is intentionally restricted to watchapps'. Touch navigation is on by default since firmware 4.33 but gated on an interaction session; watchapps are opted out unless they call app_touch_navigation_enable(true).

The official FAQ states that developing on a real watch requires a phone: the mobile app with Dev Connect enabled, then `pebble install --cloudpebble`, or the legacy Wi-Fi route `pebble install --phone IP_ADDRESS`.

`pebble install --serial` is documented as a local Bluetooth-Classic/SPP device node (e.g. /dev/cu.PebbleTimeXXXX-SerialPo) — it does not apply to PT2, whose firmware uses NimBLE (BLE only) with PPoGATT (src/fw/comm/ble/kernel_le_client/ppogatt/).

pebble-tool 5.0.39 dependencies (pyproject.toml) contain no BLE library (no bleak/dbus); available transports are qemu, websocket/phone, serial (pyserial), cloudpebble and adb. Python >= 3.10 required.
libpebble3 in the official mobile app is Kotlin Multiplatform with only android and ios targets (iOS only on macOS hosts) — no JVM/desktop target, so it cannot be run on Linux as-is.

luigi311/cobble (Rust, GPL-3.0, created 2026-06-10, last push 2026-08-23) does talk to a Pebble over BLE/PPoGATT from Linux via BlueZ, but its endpoints directory has no put_bytes.rs and no app-logs endpoint, so it cannot install a .pbw nor stream app logs.

On this machine (Ubuntu 26.04 'resolute') libSDL2-2.0.so.0 and libsndio.so.7 are missing while glib/pixman/zlib/libpng are present; `apt-get download libsdl2-2.0-0 libsndio7.0` works without root (2.32.10+dfsg-6 from main, 1.10.0-0.2 from universe), so `dpkg -x` + LD_LIBRARY_PATH is a viable no-sudo fix for the emulator.

SDK 4.33 raised the max app binary on Emery/Gabbro to 128 KiB while the loaded image and RAM footprint stay at 64 KiB each, and sizeof(ScrollLayer)/MenuLayer grew because of touch-navigation state; SDK 4.33.1 (2026-08-14) only updates the emulator, which now runs firmware 4.33.2.

recommendations: Unblock the emulator first on this no-sudo box: `mkdir -p ~/.local/debs && cd ~/.local/debs && apt-get download libsdl2-2.0-0 libsndio7.0 && for d in *.deb; do dpkg -x "$d" ~/.local/usrlibs; done && export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$HOME/.local/usrlibs/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Then `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`, `uv tool install pebble-tool==5.0.39`, `pebble sdk install latest` (4.33.1). Without SDL2+sndio, qemu-pebble will not start.

Remove 'touch UI only testable on hardware' from the risk list: touch IS emulated on `pebble-emery` (pebble_touch.c + CONFIG_TOUCH=y in boards/qemu_emery/defconfig + TOUCH_QEMU default y if SOC_QEMU).
For manual testing, just click and drag with the mouse inside the SDL window — that is a real touchdown/position-update/liftoff sequence. It is undocumented but guaranteed by the QEMU source.

For scriptable/CI touch, create a PEBBLE_QEMU_PATH wrapper that appends `-qmp unix:/tmp/pebble-qmp.sock,server=on,wait=off` to the real qemu-pebble, then write a ~50-line tools/pbltouch.py replicating pbl's cmd_touch/cmd_swipe (qmp_capabilities -> qom-list/qom-get to find pebble-touch and its display-width/height -> input-send-event with abs axes scaled to 32767 plus btn left down/up; swipe = N intermediate abs events, defaults --steps 20 --duration 0.4).

Alternative to the wrapper: launch qemu-pebble yourself with `-serial tcp::12344 -serial tcp::12345 -qmp unix:...` and attach with `pebble install build/app.pbw --qemu localhost:12344` (add `--pypkjs --platform emery` if the app has PebbleKit JS).
Do NOT design touch interactions into a watchface: SDK 4.33 forbids TouchService in watchfaces. Use the 4 buttons for the watchface and put any touch UI in a companion watchapp.

Build a screenshot-based visual regression loop (`pebble screenshot out.png`, `--gif-fps N` for animations) — this is the workflow Core Devices itself ships in pebble-watchface-agent-skill, whose default target is emery 200x228.

Test the offline path from day one with `pebble emu-bt-connection --connected no`, and consider starting the emulator already disconnected via the PEBBLE_QEMU_START_CONNECTED=0 env var read by pebble_generic.c.

Implement phone-free configuration as an on-watch MenuLayer/ActionMenu persisted with persist_* (check the runtime cap with persist_get_max_size(), added in 4.17). This is fully testable in the emulator since it runs the real firmware; do not rely on Clay/emu-app-config, which needs pypkjs/phone.

Set memory budgets now: on Emery the binary can reach 128 KiB but loaded image and RAM stay at 64 KiB each. Track with `pebble analyze-size` on every build and heap_bytes_free()/heap_bytes_used() at runtime; re-check any struct embedding ScrollLayer/MenuLayer by value, since sizeof(ScrollLayer) grew in 4.33.

Do not attempt battery or absolute-performance measurements in the emulator (stub battery with fixed values; QEMU TCG is not cycle-accurate). Use only deterministic metrics (bytes allocated, redraw counts, binary size) and relative comparisons; defer real measurements to the physical watch.

Plan on needing a phone for the first real-hardware deploy: Pebble mobile app -> Developer Mode -> Developer Connection, then `pebble install --phone <IP>` on the same Wi-Fi, or `pebble install --cloudpebble`. There is no complete Linux-only alternative today.

Also smoke-test `pebble install --emulator flint` (Pebble 2 Duo, 144x168, has_touch=false) and guard touch code with `#if defined(PBL_TOUCH)` / touch_service_is_enabled(), so the B&W target degrades gracefully.

Verify after install: `qemu-pebble -M help | grep -i pebble`, `find ~/.local/share/pebble-sdk -name 'pt2-*.png'` (to see whether SDL watch-body decorations pt2-br/pt2-sb ship with the SDK, which would also give clickable bezel buttons via `-display sdl,decoration=pt2-br`), and the QMP qom-list walk to confirm the pebble-touch device is present in the shipped binary.

gapfills.summary: Verified from primary sources (PebbleOS git history/tags, downloaded SDK tarballs, pebble-tool and mobileapp source, official docs, appstore API). A .pbw built with SDK 4.33.1 for emery/flint/gabbro is stamped sdk_version 5.106 (0x5.0x6a) and therefore runs only on PebbleOS >= v4.32.0 (GitHub release 2026-07-29). Firmware 4.10-4.16 expose minor 0x64, 4.17 -> 0x65, 4.18-4.31 (and the 4.27.1 hotfix) -> 0x66, 4.32-4.36 -> 0x6a. The minimum firmware is NOT declared anywhere: package.json sdkVersion is only "2"/"3"; the build stamps the SDK's own PROCESS_INFO_CURRENT_SDK_VERSION_MINOR (tools/waf/pebble_sdk_version.py -> manifest.json + binary header) regardless of which APIs the app uses. Neither the Core appstore (compatibility.<platform>.firmware.major=3 only) nor the phone app (platform-only isCompatible) filters by SDK minor; the watch is the sole gate. At runtime on 4.10-4.31 the app is never loaded: process_manager_check_SDK_compatible() shows the modal "Incompatible SDK / This app requires a newer version of the Pebble firmware." There is no jump-table crash, null return or no-op; the jump-table crash is exactly what the gate prevents (docs/development/sdk_export.md). Thus runtime detection of API existence is impossible and unnecessary in C; PBL_API_EXISTS is purely compile-time (defined(_PBL_API_EXISTS_##x)). Persist: the per-app quota became 1 MiB in commit 48f15c09 (first tag v4.9.171, 2026-04-30), unconditional across platforms, growable from 4 KiB, 256 B per key, E_OUT_OF_STORAGE when exhausted; persist_get_max_size() exists from v4.9.172 and is exposed by SDK 4.17+. Correct pattern: choose the SDK as the firmware floor (4.17 -> fw>=4.17.0 with persist_get_max_size/speaker/backlight/raw touch; 4.33.1 -> fw>=4.32.0 adds alarm/HRV/recognizers), use #if PBL_API_EXISTS(persist_get_max_size) with 4096 fallback, handle E_OUT_OF_STORAGE, and gate behavioral differences via watch_info_get_firmware_version() (recognizers crash before fw 4.33.2). Only SDKs 4.4, 4.5, 4.9.127, 4.9.148, 4.9.169, 4.17, 4.33.1 are downloadable.

facts.claim: On PebbleOS main (2026-08-24) PROCESS_INFO_CURRENT_SDK_VERSION_MAJOR is 0x5 and MINOR is 0x6a; the ledger comment ties 0x6a to the HRV sampling API (exported_symbols.json revision 109).
The firmware refuses to launch an app whose sdk_version.major differs or whose minor is greater than the firmware's: app_install_entry_is_SDK_compatible() requires major == and minor <=.

When the check fails, process_manager_check_SDK_compatible() logs a warning and shows an ExpandableDialog titled 'Incompatible SDK' with text 'This app requires a newer version of the Pebble firmware.'; process_manager_launch_process returns without loading the app.

PebbleOS docs state that an app built against a newer SDK would call a trampoline indexing past the end of an older firmware's g_pbl_system_tbl and crash, which is why new exports always ship as new firmware plus new SDK; function order by addedRevision is the ABI.

The SDK build stamps sdk_version from the SDK's bundled include/pebble_process_info.h (tools/waf/pebble_sdk_version.py via sdk_helpers.py) into manifest.json (process_bundle.py) and the binary header at offset 0xA (inject_metadata.py), independent of which APIs the app calls.

SDK 4.33.1 tarball stamps minor 0x6a for emery/flint/gabbro (0x56 basalt/chalk/diorite, 0x4e aplite); SDK 4.17 stamps 0x65; SDK 4.9.169 stamps 0x5f. Verified by extracting pebble_process_info.h from the official tarballs.

Minor 0x6a first appears in firmware tag v4.32.0; 0x66 (alarm_service_peek_next) in v4.18.0; 0x65 in v4.17.0; 0x63/0x64 in v4.10.0; 0x62 (backlight_service) in v4.9.175; 0x60 (persist_get_max_size) in v4.9.172; 0x5c (touch service) and 0x5e (Speaker API) in v4.9.164. v4.27.1 (hotfix of 2026-08-13) still has minor 0x66.

SDK 4.33.1 changelog (2026-08-14): fixed a crash when adding the new touch recognizers (app_touch_navigation_enable()); the emulator now runs firmware 4.33.2 which includes the fix. The only commit between v4.33.1 and v4.33.2 is 'applib/recognizer: read nav gates and ticks through syscalls'.

SDK 4.33 changelog (2026-08-12) adds tap/pan/swipe recognizers, window_attach_recognizer, app_touch_navigation_enable, window_set_touch_bridge_disabled, HealthEventHRVUpdate, health_service_peek_hrv_ppi_ms, health_service_set_hrv_sample_period, alarm_service_peek_next, raises max app binary to 128 KiB on emery/gabbro, and states Alloy apps require firmware 4.32 or later.

Per-app persistent storage is PERSIST_STORAGE_MAX_SPACE = MiBYTES(1), opened with settings_file_open_growable(max 1 MiB, initial 4 KiB), unconditional across platforms; raised from KiBYTES(6) by commit 48f15c09 (2026-02-23) whose first tag is v4.9.171. persist_get_max_size() is a syscall returning this constant.

Official Storage docs: size_t persist_get_max_size(void) 'Gets the maximum total size in bytes of all persisted values for the current app on this firmware. Apps targeting older SDKs that don't have this function should assume a 4 KB limit.'; PERSIST_DATA_MAX_LENGTH remains 256 bytes.

PBL_API_EXISTS is generated as '#define PBL_API_EXISTS(x) defined(_PBL_API_EXISTS_##x)' in pebble_sdk_version.h; it is purely a compile-time check. In SDK 4.17's emery header persist_get_max_size, speaker_*, backlight_service_subscribe and touch_service_subscribe are defined but alarm_service_peek_next, recognizers, app_touch_navigation_enable and health_service_peek_hrv_ppi_ms are not.
package.json has no minimum-firmware field: the SDK schema restricts sdkVersion to the enum ['2','3'] and the App Metadata guide lists no firmware field.

The Core appstore API exposes compatibility.<platform>.{supported, firmware:{major:3}} and hardware_platforms[].sdk_version (e.g. emery '5.95' in a real record) with only a 'hardware' query parameter; it does not filter apps by firmware minor.

The Core mobile app computes isCompatible purely from hardware platform variants (WatchType.getCompatibleAppVariants: emery accepts emery/basalt/diorite/aplite binaries, flint accepts flint/diorite/aplite) and forwards sdkVersionMajor/Minor to the watch in AppMetadata; it performs no SDK-minor vs firmware check.

pebble-tool downloads SDKs from https://sdk.repebble.com (/v1/files/sdk-core?channel=); on 2026-08-24 the server lists only 4.4, 4.5, 4.9.127, 4.9.148, 4.9.169, 4.17 and 4.33.1. Commands: pebble sdk list/install/activate/uninstall/set-channel and a per-command --sdk override.

Official install path for Linux: 'uv tool install pebble-tool' then 'pebble sdk install latest' (Python >= 3.10); emulator runtime needs apt packages libsdl2-2.0-0 libglib2.0-0 libpixman-1-0 zlib1g libsndio7.0.
SDK 4.33.1 platform defines: emery has PBL_TOUCH, PBL_RGB_BACKLIGHT, PBL_SPEAKER, 200x228, 128 KiB app binary/memory; flint has PBL_SPEAKER but no PBL_TOUCH/PBL_RGB_BACKLIGHT, 144x168, 64 KiB.

watch_info_get_firmware_version() returns WatchInfoVersion {uint8_t major, minor, patch} and is available in all SDKs considered, making it the runtime probe for firmware-dependent behaviour (e.g. recognizer crash before 4.33.2).

recommendations: Set the firmware floor by choosing the SDK, not by code: SDK 4.17 => PebbleOS >= 4.17.0 (has persist_get_max_size, speaker, backlight service, raw touch, quick-launch args); SDK 4.33.1 => PebbleOS >= 4.32.0 (adds alarm_service_peek_next, HRV, recognizers, app_touch_navigation_enable). For offline-first watchfaces/apps that do not need alarm/HRV/recognizers, ship the SDK 4.17 build until the installed base has migrated.

Do not attempt runtime detection of API existence in C: it is impossible (no dynamic lookup) and unnecessary (the watch refuses to launch apps with a newer SDK minor). Use PBL_API_EXISTS() only to keep one source buildable on multiple SDKs.

Size the local cache on persist_get_max_size() at runtime (1 MiB on all PebbleOS >= 4.9.171) with '#if PBL_API_EXISTS(persist_get_max_size) ... #else return 4096; #endif', chunk blobs into 256-byte records (PERSIST_DATA_MAX_LENGTH), keep an index/schema-version key, budget <= ~75% of the quota, and always handle E_OUT_OF_STORAGE / negative status_t from persist_write_*.

If you use gesture recognizers with SDK 4.33.1, gate window_attach_recognizer()/app_touch_navigation_enable() behind watch_info_get_firmware_version() >= 4.33.2 (crash on 4.32-4.33.1), or use raw touch_service_subscribe() which has been stable since fw 4.9.164.

Guard platform features with the SDK defines (PBL_TOUCH, PBL_SPEAKER, PBL_RGB_BACKLIGHT, PBL_PLATFORM_FLINT) and runtime checks (touch_service_is_enabled(), speaker_is_muted()) since flint has no touch/RGB backlight and users can disable touch.

Install user-locally without sudo: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh; uv tool install pebble-tool; pebble sdk install 4.33.1; pebble sdk install 4.17; pebble sdk activate 4.17 (or pebble build --sdk 4.33.1). Building works without root; verify whether the QEMU emulator runs without the apt SDL2/glib/pixman/sndio libraries.

Test the incompatibility path locally: build with 4.33.1 and install on the SDK 4.17 emulator (firmware 4.17) to see the 'Incompatible SDK' dialog; build with 4.17 and run on the 4.33.1 emulator (firmware 4.33.2) to confirm forward compatibility.
State the required PebbleOS version explicitly in appstore release notes ('Requires PebbleOS 4.32+' or '4.17+'), because neither the store nor the phone app shows or filters on it.

Watch the append-only ledger in src/fw/process_management/pebble_process_info.h and the SDK changelog page before every SDK upgrade: recompiling with a newer SDK raises the floor for the whole app even if no new API is used.
